title: क्लाइमेट चेंज ने बढ़ाया तापमान, स्पेन में 20 गुना बढ़ी जंगलों की आग - AajTak

full_text:
क्लाइमेट चेंज का असर अब सिर्फ बढ़ती गर्मी तक सीमित नहीं है. नई स्टडी में पता चला है कि इसकी वजह से स्पेन और फ्रांस में जंगलों में आग फैलाने वाला मौसम पहले से ज्यादा खतरनाक हो गया है. वैज्ञानिकों ने पुराने मौसम के रिकॉर्ड और आज के मौसम की तुलना की. Photo: AP
इसमें पता चला कि इंसानों की वजह से बढ़ रही ग्लोबल वॉर्मिंग ने स्पेन के बीच वाले हिस्से में ऐसे हालात 20 गुना और फ्रांस के दक्षिण-पश्चिम हिस्से में 2 गुना बढ़ा दिए हैं. यही वजह है कि इन इलाकों में जंगल की आग तेजी से फैल रही है और उसे बुझाना मुश्किल हो रहा है. Photo: AP
स्पेन और फ्रांस में इस समय कई जगह जंगलों में भीषण आग लगी हुई है. आग की वजह से बड़ी संख्या में लोगों को अपने घर छोड़ने पड़े हैं और हजारों हेक्टेयर जंगल जल चुके हैं. Photo: AP
वैज्ञानिकों का कहना है कि जब बहुत ज्यादा गर्मी, लंबे समय तक सूखा और तेज हवा एक साथ होती है, तब आग बहुत तेजी से फैलती है. ऐसे मौसम को 'फायर वेदर' यानी आग फैलाने वाला मौसम कहा जाता है. Photo: AP
यह स्टडी वर्ल्ड वेदर एट्रिब्यूशन (World Weather Attribution) के वैज्ञानिकों ने की है. इसमें पुराने और नए मौसम के आंकड़ों की तुलना की गई. अब दक्षिण-पश्चिम फ्रांस में ऐसे हालात करीब 20 साल में एक बार बन सकते हैं. वहीं, स्पेन के बीच वाले हिस्से में ऐसे हालात हर 6 साल में एक बार बनने की आशंका है. Photo: AP
वैज्ञानिकों का कहना है कि अब पहले के मुकाबले ज्यादा बार ऐसा मौसम बन रहा है, जिसमें गर्मी ज्यादा होती है, बारिश कम होती है और तेज हवा चलती है. ऐसे में अगर कहीं छोटी सी भी आग लग जाए, तो वह जल्दी ही बड़े जंगल में फैल सकती है. Photo: AP
WMO के मुताबिक, धरती का औसत तापमान अब पहले के मुकाबले करीब 1.4 डिग्री सेल्सियस बढ़ चुका है. इसकी बड़ी वजह कोयला, तेल और गैस का लगातार इस्तेमाल है. इसी कारण दुनिया में हीटवेव, सूखा और जंगलों में आग जैसी घटनाएं भी बढ़ रही हैं. Photo: AP
वैज्ञानिकों ने यह भी बताया कि अब यूरोप में एक नया पैटर्न देखने को मिल रहा है. सर्दियों में अच्छी बारिश होने से जंगलों में खूब घास और पेड़-पौधे उग जाते हैं. लेकिन जब गर्मियों में तेज गर्मी और सूखा पड़ता है, तो यही घास और पेड़-पौधे सूखकर आग के लिए ईंधन बन जाते हैं. इसलिए आग लगने पर वह बहुत तेजी से फैलती है. Photo: AP
इस साल स्पेन में जनवरी का महीना पिछले 25 साल का सबसे ज्यादा बारिश वाला रहा. इसके बाद वहां रिकॉर्ड गर्मी पड़ी. वहीं, फ्रांस इस साल अब तक चार बार हीटवेव झेल चुका है. वैज्ञानिकों का कहना है कि इन दोनों वजहों से जंगलों में आग लगने और फैलने का खतरा और बढ़ गया. Photo: Reuters
वैज्ञानिकों का कहना है कि सिर्फ आग बुझाना ही काफी नहीं है. जंगलों से सूखी घास और सूखे पेड़-पौधों को पहले ही हटाना होगा और ऐसी तैयारी करनी होगी जिससे आग फैलने का खतरा कम हो. उनका कहना है कि अगर ग्रीनहाउस गैसों को कम नहीं किया गया, तो आने वाले समय में जंगलों में आग की ऐसी घटनाएं और बढ़ सकती हैं. Photo: Reuters

अच्छी नींद के लिए शरीर का तापमान थोड़ा कम होना जरूरी है. लेकिन जब रात भी गर्म रहती है, तो शरीर ठंडा नहीं हो पाता.
नई दिल्लीः बढ़ता तापमान, घटती नींद और बढ़ती चिंता ने सभी को परेशान किया है. क्लाइमेट सेंट्रल के विश्लेषण के अनुसार, 2020 से 2025 के बीच दुनिया के 1,338 शहरों में लोगों ने बढ़ती गर्म रातों के कारण औसतन हर वर्ष 56 घंटे की नींद गंवाई. इनमें से लगभग 6 घंटे की कमी सीधे मानव-जनित जलवायु परिवर्तन से जुड़ी है. पिछले 50 वर्षों में यह नुकसान लगभग दोगुना हो चुका है.
भारत पर सबसे ज्यादा असर
भारत इस संकट से सबसे अधिक प्रभावित देशों में है. 107 भारतीय शहरों के विश्लेषण में पाया गया कि दक्षिण भारत के कई शहरों में लोग हर साल 78 से 91 घंटे तक नींद खो रहे हैं. चेन्नई, मुंबई, कोलकाता और बेंगलुरु जैसे महानगरों में गर्म और उमस भरी रातें अब स्वास्थ्य के लिए गंभीर चुनौती बन चुकी हैं.

-नींद आने में देर लगती है
-सुबह भी थकान बनी रहती है.
नींद की कमी के गंभीर परिणाम
लगातार कम नींद लेने से कई स्वास्थ्य समस्याओं का खतरा बढ़ जाता है : उच्च रक्तचाप और हृदय रोग, मधुमेह और मोटापा, अवसाद व चिंता, कमजोर प्रतिरक्षा, याददाश्त और कार्यक्षमता में कमी.
इसका असर सड़क दुर्घटनाओं, कार्यस्थल की उत्पादकता और छात्रों की सीखने की क्षमता पर भी पड़ता है.
शहर रात में भी क्यों नहीं ठंडे होते?
कांक्रीट के बढ़ते जंगल, घटते हरित क्षेत्र और अर्बन हीट आइलैंड प्रभाव शहरों को रात में भी गर्म बनाए रखते हैं. अधिक प्रभावित वे लोग हैं जिनके घरों में एयर कंडीशनर, पर्याप्त वेंटिलेशन या खुली जगह नहीं है.
समाधान क्या है?
सिर्फ एयर कंडीशनर इस समस्या का स्थायी हल नहीं है. विशेषज्ञ शहरों में हरित क्षेत्र बढ़ाने, जलाशयों के संरक्षण, कम गर्मी सोखने वाली निर्माण सामग्री, बेहतर वेंटिलेशन और ग्रीनहाउस गैसों के उत्सर्जन में कमी पर जोर देते हैं. जलवायु परिवर्तन अब भविष्य की नहीं, वर्तमान की चुनौती है.
जब गर्म रातें हमारी नींद, सेहत और मानसिक संतुलन छीनने लगें, तो यह केवल मौसम का बदलाव नहीं रह जाता. यदि अभी प्रभावी कदम नहीं उठाए गए, तो अधूरी नींद और गर्म रातें हमारी नई सामान्य जीवनशैली बन सकती हैं.’

full_text:
Modern homes in hot climates often depend on air conditioning to remain comfortable, but a newly completed residence in
Maharashtra takes a different approach. The Anthill House uses thick masonry, shaded courts, air circulation and not artificial cooling. The flowing plan of the house draws inspiration from the underground structures of the anthills, where little ants have developed a technique for making their surroundings habitable regardless of changes in external weather. Although the building is a piece of contemporary architecture, its biological concept is backed up by scientific evidence, which states that the ants change the depth and intricacy of their nests in accordance with temperature conditions.
The design draws inspiration from the way ants respond to changing temperatures
Unlike many buildings that rely on sealed interiors and mechanical cooling, the Anthill House embraces passive design.
Its interconnected rooms, shaded courtyards, perforated brick walls and carefully positioned openings encourage natural airflow throughout the building. Thick brick walls also act as thermal mass, absorbing heat during the day and releasing it gradually as outdoor temperatures fall, helping moderate indoor conditions.
The layout echoes the branching chambers and tunnels found beneath an ant nest, where movement of air and the surrounding soil together create a more stable microclimate.
Scientists found that ants change their nest architecture as temperatures change
The biological inspiration behind the project is reflected in the study ‘
Ant Nest Architecture Is Shaped by Local Adaptation and Plastic Response to Temperature’ by Madison Sankovitz and Jessica Purcell.
The researchers investigated colonies of Formica podzolica collected from different elevations in Colorado and exposed them to two soil-surface temperature treatments. Instead of constructing nests in the same way, the ants tailored the structure of their nests in the underground according to their experience.
The colonies that were subjected to higher surface temperature built nests that were significantly deeper, while the size and complexity of their tunnel networks were influenced by the combination of the temperature and the climate of the origin of those ants. The experiment resulted in the conclusion that the nest architecture is not only plastic, but also locally adapted.
Ant nests regulate more than temperature
The authors make sure to stress that the underground nest is more than just a shelter. The depth of the nest determines the microclimate in which the colony lives, as the temperature, humidity, and air composition differ depending on the depth in the soil. According to the research, the digging of deep nests under warm weather conditions can assist colonies in avoiding too much heat at the surface, while shallow nests can have advantages under cold conditions.
Contrary to the traditional blueprints that one uses to build their house, ants continuously alter the nest according to changes in the conditions, thus making it a perfect example of the extended phenotype described by biologists.
Nature's engineering continues to inspire sustainable architecture
Anthill House does not simply copy ant nests. Instead, it uses the very same idea by working with the weather conditions instead of fighting them.
With the help of passive cooling, shading, thermal mass and room connections, the house minimizes the need for artificial cooling while being in harmony with its warm environment. Though the scientific paper does not consider the architecture of buildings and only discusses ants, it shows that adaptive architectural solutions can help to improve thermal characteristics without using intensive mechanical systems.
As Sankovitz and Purcell note in their article, nest architecture is an adaptable solution to weather conditions and not an inflexible one. The same principle is used when designing climate-responsive buildings, which means that instead of intensive cooling systems, architects should use natural adaptation to weather conditions.

LONDON, Jul 30 : The UK's heatwave related deaths are set for record highs this summer, with health authorities reporting a near doubling of figures in just two months compared to the previous year on Thursday.
The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) said its "rapid early assessment" indicates there were 2,877 heat-associated deaths during notable periods of hot weather in May and June, almost double the 1,504 reported annually for 2025, with the data coming at a time when authorities declared a drought for half of England this week.
While these figures remain interim as there have been further heatwaves over the course of the ongoing summer months in the country, they are already approaching the annual record reported by UKHSA in 2022.
"Based on the interim data, it is likely that 2026 could see the highest number of heat-associated deaths on record, surpassing the 2,985 recorded in 2022," the UKHSA said.
Dr Ross Thompson, Principal Environmental Public Health Scientist at UKHSA and author of the interim report, said: "These figures highlight the significant danger that very hot weather can pose to people's health. This is particularly true for those who are more vulnerable including older adults and people with underlying medical conditions."
"While the figures are interim, they suggest that, if we experience more periods of hot weather this summer, we could see the highest number of heat-associated deaths on record," he added.
An estimated 753 deaths were associated with the May heat episode and a further 2,124 with the June heatwave in the UK.
The data comes as authorities declared a drought for half of England this week, following the persistent high temperatures and record-low rainfall. Many regions of the country are also under a hosepipe ban to conserve water during exceptionally dry weather since earlier this year.
The UK's June heatwave lasted for eight days and triggered a red heat-health alert. This was only the second time the highest level of alert has been issued in England, reflecting the exceptional temperatures recorded.
Both May and June also broke Met Office monthly temperature records for England with 31.5 degrees Celsius recorded on May 26 and 37.7 degrees Celsius recorded on June 26.
The health agency said its findings demonstrate the importance of the heat-health alerting system, delivered in partnership with the Meteorological (Met) Office, which provides early warning when temperatures are likely to have significant impacts on health and wellbeing.
Heatwaves occurring earlier in the season can have a greater impact due to people, communities and services having less time to adapt to the warmer conditions, it cautioned.
"The sweltering heat has had a serious impact this summer on people's health and on our NHS [National Health Service]," said UK Health and Social Care Secretary Yvette Cooper.
"For many years, we have been used to winter pressures in our NHS and the need to support those who are vulnerable in the coldest weather. But now we are seeing the summer heat have an increasingly serious impact on the health of thousands of people, and on the pressures facing our NHS too," she said.
Not just the UK, according to the World Meteorological Organisation (WMO), June saw much of western Europe experiencing a record-breaking heatwave and marine heatwaves across the western Mediterranean and along the Atlantic coasts.
June 2026 was the hottest June recorded for western Europe and the second warmest globally, driven by the highest sea surface temperatures (SSTs) on record for the month, WMO said. (PTI)

Super Typhoon Dolphin is approaching Korea, with its track expected to be a key factor in determining whether the extreme heat wave continues into next week.
Dolphin, the 13th named storm of the season, is moving west-northwest at 25 kilometers (16 miles) per hour over waters about 1,910 kilometers east of Guam as of 9 a.m. Friday, the Korea Meteorological Administration (KMA) said. The storm had a central pressure of 905 millibars and maximum sustained winds of 56 meters (184 feet) per second, placing it at Level 5, the highest intensity on the KMA's five-tier scale.
Dolphin is currently the strongest typhoon to form this year. Satellite images show a well-defined eye, underscoring its intensity.
The storm is forecast to continue moving west and reach waters about 1,000 kilometers east of Okinawa, Japan on Wednesday. Although it is expected to weaken slightly to Level 4 by then, maximum sustained winds are still forecast to reach 49 meters per second.
Its path after that remains highly uncertain. However, meteorologists say the storm's trajectory could significantly affect the extreme heat that has gripped the country.
A strong heat dome has formed over the Korean Peninsula as the North Pacific High and the Tibetan High remain in place. If those high-pressure systems persist, Dolphin is more likely to track toward China along the edge of the ridge.
"The easterly wind pattern created as the typhoon passes to the south will affect Korea," said Kang Nam-young, a geography professor at Kyungpook National University. "As moisture-laden easterly winds cross the Taebaek mountain range, they will warm further, which could intensify the heat wave in western regions."
If the high-pressure system covering the Korean Peninsula weakens after next week, the typhoon could instead turn northward. That would likely ease the heat wave, but increase the risk of torrential rain and damaging winds.
"The typhoon is so large that, if it enters Korea, it could cause damage on the scale of Typhoon Rusa," Kang said, referring to the typhoon that hit Korea in 2002. "By early next week, we should have a clearer picture of its projected path."
Extreme heat is expected to continue Friday, with temperatures reaching as high as 40 degrees Celsius (104 degrees Fahrenheit) in parts of South Gyeongsang.
Sunny weather is forecast to persist through the weekend and into next week, with the heat wave expected to peak nationwide. Temperatures in the Seoul metropolitan area are also expected to climb as high as 37 degrees Celsius.
"For the time being, the maximum heat index will rise to around 35 degrees Celsius across most parts of the country, and many areas will continue to experience tropical nights," a KMA official said. "Heat-related illnesses are possible, and people need to drink plenty of water and avoid strenuous outdoor activities."

The heatwave is failing to boost sales of air conditioners: down by 150,000 units so far in 2026
According to figures from Assoclima, the first half of the year saw a decline in production
The heatwave has failed to boost sales of air conditioners. On the contrary: the first half of 2026 ended on a negative note for one of the summer season’s iconic products. The figure emerges from the statistical survey by Assoclima (the association of air-conditioning system manufacturers affiliated with Anima Confindustria), covering the period from January to June.
Single-split and multi-split air-conditioning units, therefore, have seen a decline in both volume and value compared with the same period in 2025. It should be emphasised that this is one of the most significant segments of this market: in the first half of the year, around 1,650,000 units were sold, generating a turnover of just over 1.2 billion euros. These are huge figures, but lower than last year’s.
In particular, single-split systems recorded a fall of 9.8 per cent by volume and 7.8 per cent by value, whilst multi-split systems limited the decline to 5.5 per cent by volume and 6.9 per cent by value. Bucking the trend, among others, were multi-split systems with domestic hot water production, which rose by 25.5 per cent in volume and 14.4 per cent in value. Overall, around 150,000 fewer units were sold compared with last year.
There are several factors behind these figures: ‘Air conditioning,’ says a statement from the association, ‘remains an impulse purchase, heavily influenced by weather conditions.’ In other words, many consumers do not yet consider the various functions a heat pump can serve, but focus on cooling. The figures for 2026 were therefore influenced by a weather pattern that differed from that of 2025. “After a start to the year characterised by weak demand,” the statement continues, “the intense heat only arrived in the second half of June, by which time the first-half survey was already drawing to a close.” The recovery in orders and the subsequent restocking of the distribution network “were concentrated between the end of June and July, suggesting a possible recovery in the third-quarter figures”.
However, there are other factors to consider as well. The sector’s performance has also been influenced by the comparison with 2025, a year characterised by particularly dynamic market conditions, ‘the level of remaining stock throughout the supply chain’, greater caution in purchasing on the part of retailers, and ‘the continuing economic uncertainty faced by households, exacerbated by energy costs’.

13 Gujarat Districts Under Red Alert on July 31

District Collectors have been given the authority to take decisions on school and anganwadi closures depending on the local rainfall situation.
